samples.summary: `printable()` strips only C0/C1 controls, leaving bidi overrides and invisible Unicode able to misrender the findings report
samples.evidence: `printable` is the sanitizer for model-written `summary`/`file`/`line`/`lens` on the one screen a developer reads to decide whether the branch is clean (its docblock: "the text could hide the findings printed above it or forge a 'no blocking findings' line"). The character class `/[�--]/` defuses ANSI CSI (which needs ESC) and the `\s+` collapse prevents line forging (JS `\s` covers U+2028/U+2029). But nothing handles U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE / U+202D LRO, the U+2066–U+2069 isolates, U+200B–U+200D zero-widths, or the U+E0000–U+E007F tag block. A finding whose `summary` embeds an RLO renders in most terminals with the trailing text visually reversed, and tag/zero-width characters are invisible entirely — so a finding can be made to read as something other than its bytes on the decision surface. Attack: a lens (or a prompt-injected diff steering one) emits `summary: "benign nit‮..."`; the developer reads a line that does not correspond to the recorded finding. Defense-in-depth on a display path, hence minor, but the function's stated contract is "made safe to print".

samples.summary: The local `--rebuttals` path applies no length or count caps, unlike every other route into the adjudicator prompt
samples.evidence: `readRebuttalRecords` (spec-to-pr.mjs:663-673) parses the file and hands it to `normalizeRebuttals` (:632-636), which by its own docblock touches only the `agent-review-` lens prefix. The cloud route caps every author-written field at serialization — `rebuttal.mjs:99-110`: `findingKey` 300, `lens` 60, `file` 300, `summary` 2000, `claim` 4000, `evidence` max 10 entries x 500 — with the explicit reasoning "The writer is the untrusted party, so a cap applied only on read would still let it post a megabyte comment". The local file skips that writer entirely and goes straight to `review-panel.mjs:2662-2665`, which only filters for objects. It also skips `neutral()` (the `<!--` ZWNJ split), and no cap bounds the number of records, each of which buys a 20-turn adjudicator session (`ADJUDICATOR_MAX_TURNS`). Vector: the record file is written by the same agent that is under review (per `.claude/commands/self-review.md`, step 2 "Dispute it"), so unbounded self-authored text reaches the one component that can remove a finding from the gate, plus unbounded session spend. Held to minor because I confirmed the load-bearing control still fires: `buildAdjudicatorPrompt` applies `defence()` to `r.claim` and each `r.evidence` at render time (rebuttal.mjs:492-494), so the `</author-rebuttal>` fence-escape is neutralized regardless of which route the record took.

samples.summary: `realpathSync` erases symlinked intermediates before the ancestor walk, so a foreign-owned symlink ancestor is never inspected despite the guard claiming it checks "every ancestor, and whoever made it"
samples.evidence: The call site comment at :886-890 states the rule as "EVERY ANCESTOR, not just the leaf, and whoever made it", and :938 walks `ownedPathChain(path.dirname(base), ...)` where `base = realpathSync(requested)` (:936). Because the chain is the *resolved* one, the unresolved components are gone: if another user owns `<tmp>/wafflebase-self-review` as a symlink, that symlink and its owner are never `lstat`ed by any branch of this code — the leaf check at :916 uses `lstatSync(requested)`, which follows intermediate symlinks and only refuses a symlinked *final* component. The resolution to `/var` -> `/private/var` on macOS is the legitimate case that motivated it, but it also blinds the guard to an attacker-planted intermediate. I could not escalate this to a real compromise: the attacker chooses the target, but `mkdirSync` then creates our leaf there at 0700 owned by us, and the resolved ancestors are still checked, so a target under an attacker-owned or foreign-writable-non-sticky directory is refused at :944. The residue is that a third party can silently relocate the review store to any directory owned by root or by us (e.g. the developer's own 0700 `~/.config`), creating `<branch>-<hash>/round-N/pr.diff` at a path of their choosing rather than the documented one. Confidentiality and integrity of the contents survive; the discrepancy between the guard's claim and its coverage is what I am reporting.

samples.summary: The review base is created before any of its ownership/mode/symlink validation runs
samples.evidence: `mkdirSync(requested, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` at :904 executes before the leaf `lstat` (:916), the leaf rule (:918), the `realpathSync` (:936) and the ancestor walk (:938-945). With `recursive: true` this also creates intermediates. So when an attacker has pre-created `<tmp>/wafflebase-self-review` as a symlink or as their own directory, the process has already created a directory through it by the time the guard fires and exits 1. No data is written — every `writeFileSync` on this path is below the guard — so the impact is confined to unauthorized directory creation at an attacker-influenced path, which is why this is minor rather than a write-redirect. Validating the parent (or creating with `mkdirSync(..., { recursive: false })` per level, checking as it descends) would close the ordering rather than rely on the refusal arriving second.

samples.summary: Contributor docs advertise `@claude loop` without stating it requires write access and refuses fork PRs
samples.evidence: The new text tells the reader to "Comment `@claude review` for an advisory panel run (once per commit), or `@claude loop` to opt into the panel plus its auto-fix rounds" (CONTRIBUTING.md, new step 3 block), and CLAUDE.md line 65 repeats it as "`@claude loop` (panel + auto-fix)". The enforced gate is stricter on both axes: `.github/workflows/agent-loop.yml:72-77` calls `getCollaboratorPermissionLevel` and `core.setFailed` unless the commenter holds `admin`/`maintain`/`write`, and :122-128 refuses any fork PR outright. CONTRIBUTING.md is the document aimed at outside contributors — the population that satisfies neither condition. The design doc's table (docs/design/agentic-dev-loop.md §1.1) gets halfway there with "same-repo only" but still omits the write-access requirement. The gate itself is correctly enforced, so this is documentation of a privilege boundary rather than a bypass; the cost is contributors invoking a privileged trigger they cannot use and misreading who is permitted to drive the auto-fix loop.

samples.summary: Removing the credential gate means the command now spends the ambient logged-in session with an advisory notice and no confirmation
samples.evidence: `cmdReview` previously returned early when `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` was absent; it now emits `ambientAuthNotice` (:865-866) and proceeds, so `review-panel.mjs` spawns multi-lens sessions against whatever credentials the SDK resolves. The notice says so explicitly ("bills the account you are logged in as") and the docblock at :253-262 argues the case well — a silent skip that reads as a pass is genuinely worse. Recording it only for coverage: an agent following `.claude/commands/self-review.md` invokes this with no interactive confirmation step, so credential use is now automatic where it was previously opt-in. I verified the blast radius is bounded: the sessions get read-only `REVIEW_TOOLS` (review-panel.mjs:2006, :2247, :2521), no token is interpolated into `panelArgs`, and no workflow or package script invokes `spec-to-pr.mjs review`, so CI behaviour is unchanged.
